claim: TBX5 is a cardiac transcription factor that regulates a network of cardiac channel genes to maintain cardiac rhythm.
source: TBX5, a cardiac TF, regulates a network of cardiac channel genes to maintain cardiac rhythm.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as background information for the study.

claim: Approximately 2600 novel Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were identified by deep sequencing wildtype and Tbx5-mutant mouse atria.
source: We deep sequenced wildtype and Tbx5-mutant mouse atria, identifying ~2600 novel Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract based on the RNA sequencing experiments performed.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were enriched for tissue-specific marks of active enhancers genome-wide.
source: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were enriched for tissue-specific marks of active enhancers genome-wide.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data shown in Figure 1E-F and Figure 2A.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs emanated from regions that are enriched for TBX5-binding.
source: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs emanated from regions that are enriched for TBX5-binding and that demonstrated Tbx5-dependent enhancer activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2F.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs emanated from regions that demonstrated Tbx5-dependent enhancer activity.
source: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs emanated from regions that are enriched for TBX5-binding and that demonstrated Tbx5-dependent enhancer activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by luciferase assays shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNA transcription provided a quantitative metric of Tbx5-dependent enhancer activity, correlating with target gene expression.
source: Tbx5-dependent ncRNA transcription provided a quantitative metric of Tbx5-dependent enhancer activity, correlating with target gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B-C.

claim: RACER is a novel Tbx5-dependent long noncoding RNA required for the expression of the calcium-handling gene Ryr2.
source: We identified RACER, a novel Tbx5-dependent long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) required for the expression of the calcium-handling gene Ryr2.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: TF-dependent enhancer transcription can illuminate components of TF-dependent gene regulatory networks.
source: We illustrate that TF-dependent enhancer transcription can illuminate components of TF-dependent gene regulatory networks.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: Cardiac rhythm is under tight transcriptional control.
source: Cardiac rhythm is under tight transcriptional control (e.g. Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Mendelian and genome-wide association genetic studies have implicated cardiac ion channels and transcription factors in cardiac conduction and arrhythmias.
source: Mendelian and genome-wide association genetic studies have implicated cardiac ion channels and transcription factors (TFs) in cardiac conduction and arrhythmias (Tucker and Ellinor, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: TBX5 is required for normal cardiac rhythm.
source: TBX5 is a central component of cardiac gene regulatory networks and is required for normal cardiac rhythm (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: TBX5 modulates atrial gene expression to prevent atrial fibrillation.
source: For example, we previously demonstrated that TBX5 modulates atrial gene expression to prevent atrial fibrillation (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Over 15,000 common genomic locations were identified by intersecting DNase I hypersensitivity, H3K27Ac, and TBX5 occupancy data.
source: Over 15,000 common genomic locations were identified.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the intersection of multiple genomic datasets shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Intersection of ATAC-seq data with other datasets identified over 7500 common genomic locations.
source: We also performed ATAC-seq in HL-1 cells, and intersection with this more limited dataset (with 16,000 accessible regions) identified over 7500 common genomic locations.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Genomic enhancer marks and TF ChIP lack specificity or quantitative resolution of enhancer strength.
source: The high concordance between these datasets suggested a lack of specificity for functional TBX5-dependent enhancers, consistent with observations that genomic enhancer marks and TF ChIP lack specificity or quantitative resolution of enhancer strength (Zentner and Scacheri, 2012)
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation support.

claim: Only a small percentage of candidate TF-dependent enhancers will prove to be functional in-vivo.
source: consistent with observations that genomic enhancer marks and TF ChIP lack specificity or quantitative resolution of enhancer strength (Zentner and Scacheri, 2012) and that only a small percentage of these candidate TF-dependent enhancers will prove to be functional in-vivo (Visel et al., 2007; Cusanovich et al., 2014; Danko et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation support.

claim: The noncoding genome is pervasively transcribed.
source: The noncoding genome is pervasively transcribed.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: A fraction of ncRNAs emanate from enhancers.
source: The noncoding genome is pervasively transcribed, and a fraction of ncRNAs emanate from enhancers.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Enhancer transcription may be a functional requirement of active enhancers.
source: Recent work indicates that enhancer transcription may be a functional requirement of active enhancers (Danko et al., 2015; Lam et al., 2014; Li et al., 2013, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: The level of eRNA expression at enhancers positively correlates with the level of mRNA synthesis at nearby genes.
source: The level of eRNA expression at enhancers positively correlates with the level of mRNA synthesis at nearby genes, suggesting that eRNA synthesis may occur specifically at enhancers that are actively engaged in promoting mRNA synthesis (Kim et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Activation of enhancer networks has been linked to the increased transcription of enhancers.
source: Activation of enhancer networks has been linked to the increased transcription of enhancers, suggesting that context-dependent changes in enhancer function may be accompanied by concomitant changes in enhancer transcription (Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Tissue-specific eRNA expression is a feature of some validated in-vivo enhancers.
source: Tissue-specific eRNA expression is a feature of some validated in-vivo enhancers, and eRNA expression signatures can be used to predict tissue-specific enhancers independently of known epigenomic enhancer marks (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: eRNA expression signatures can be used to predict tissue-specific enhancers independently of known epigenomic enhancer marks.
source: Tissue-specific eRNA expression is a feature of some validated in-vivo enhancers, and eRNA expression signatures can be used to predict tissue-specific enhancers independently of known epigenomic enhancer marks (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Approximately 40.5k noncoding transcripts were identified by de novo transcript assembly.
source: Approximately 40.5 k noncoding transcripts were identified by de novo transcript assembly (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 3610 noncoding transcripts were Tbx5-dependent intergenic ncRNAs.
source: Of these, 3610 noncoding transcripts were Tbx5-dependent intergenic ncRNAs (FDR < 0.05, FC > 1.5, located at least 1 kbp away from known coding-gene transcription start sites (TSSs) (ENCODE mm10; Figure 1B) (Rosenbloom et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific statistical criteria and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNA expression was robust across biological replicates, distinguishing Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERt2 samples from R26CreERt2 controls.
source: Tbx5-dependent ncRNA expression was robust across biological replicates, distinguishing Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERt2 samples from R26CreERt2 controls (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in the heatmap in Figure 1C.

claim: 3067 (85%) Tbx5-dependent ncRNA transcripts were located within 2 Mbp upstream or downstream of 2383 Tbx5-dependent protein-coding genes.
source: 3067 (85%) Tbx5-dependent ncRNA transcripts were located within 2 Mbp upstream or downstream of 2383 Tbx5-dependent protein-coding genes, as defined by the RNA-seq of polyA transcripts from the same samples, that is, within the known distance parameters of enhancer–gene-target pairs (Figure 1D) (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific numbers and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The vast majority of Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were de novo ncRNAs (>85% were previously unannotated transcripts).
source: The vast majority were de novo ncRNAs (>85% were previously unannotated transcripts, based on intersection with the mouse transcriptome [GENECODE, mm10]), with a small number previously annotated as long ncRNAs (lncRNAs, 5%), antisense transcripts (2%), or other predicted noncoding transcripts.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the genomic features of Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs showed a bimodal length-distribution, with relative enrichments at ~500 bp and at ~2000 bp.
source: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs showed a bimodal length-distribution, with relative enrichments at ~500 bp and at ~2000 bp (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), similar to the distribution of GENCODE-annotated lncRNAs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The 40.5k ncRNA background and Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs both show a preponderance of unidirectional versus bidirectional transcripts.
source: The 40.5 k ncRNA background and Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs both show a preponderance of unidirectional (transcribed from one DNA strand) versus bidirectional transcripts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Sequence conservation indicated average Phastcon30 scores of between 0 and 0.2 for the majority of Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs.
source: Sequence conservation indicated average Phastcon30 scores of between 0 and 0.2 for the majority of Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs, with a distribution similar to those of known lncRNAs and lower than those of promoters (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were generated from locations enriched for DNAse hypersensitivity in the adult mouse heart.
source: Specifically, we observed enrichment between the 3067 Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs and (1) DNAse hypersensitivity in the adult mouse heart, (2) open chromatin (ATAC-sequencing) in HL1 cardiomyocytes, and (3) H3K27Ac in the adult mouse heart (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) (He et al., 2011, 2014; Wamstad et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1E-F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were generated from locations enriched for open chromatin (ATAC-sequencing) in HL1 cardiomyocytes.
source: Specifically, we observed enrichment between the 3067 Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs and (1) DNAse hypersensitivity in the adult mouse heart, (2) open chromatin (ATAC-sequencing) in HL1 cardiomyocytes, and (3) H3K27Ac in the adult mouse heart (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) (He et al., 2011, 2014; Wamstad et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1E-F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were generated from locations enriched for H3K27Ac in the adult mouse heart.
source: Specifically, we observed enrichment between the 3067 Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs and (1) DNAse hypersensitivity in the adult mouse heart, (2) open chromatin (ATAC-sequencing) in HL1 cardiomyocytes, and (3) H3K27Ac in the adult mouse heart (Figure 1E–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) (He et al., 2011, 2014; Wamstad et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1E-F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs defined locations that are enriched genome-wide for TBX5 occupancy in HL-1 cells.
source: Furthermore, Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs defined locations that are enriched genome-wide for TBX5 occupancy in HL-1 cells (He et al., 2011) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 1703 candidate regulatory elements were identified by the intersection of differential ncRNA expression with cardiac DNAse hypersensitivity.
source: 1703 candidate regulatory elements, from a set of 28,393 TBX5-bound DNAse regions, were identified by this intersection (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 11 of the 12 candidate enhancers demonstrated robust cis-activity in HL-1 cardiomyocytes.
source: 11 of the 12 candidate enhancers demonstrated robust cis-activity in HL-1 cardiomyocytes, indicative of cardiac enhancer function (P-values from 3.3e-6 to 0.03 [t-test, corrected for multiple comparisons], Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical values and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Nine enhancers drove reporter expression more than 10-fold and three more than 50-fold.
source: Overall, these enhancers demonstrated unusually strong cis-activation, with nine driving reporter expression more than 10-fold and three more than 50-fold.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the luciferase assay results.

claim: The activity of 10 of the 11 enhancers was significantly diminished by mutation of their canonical T-box sites.
source: These enhancers were strongly TBX5-dependent, as the activity of 10 of the 11 enhancers was significantly diminished by mutation of their canonical T-box sites (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Tbx5-dependent transcription increased the predictive power of DNAse hypersensitivity, H3K27 acetylation, and open chromatin by ATAC-Seq (>2 fold for precision, with similar specificity).
source: Tbx5-dependent transcription increased the predictive power of DNAse hypersensitivity (DHS), H3K27 acetylation, and open chromatin by ATAC-Seq (>2 fold for precision, with similar specificity, Figure 2D)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: 145 local Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs marking 152 candidate Tbx5-dependent enhancers were identified from 16,000 open regions.
source: From 16,000 open regions, we identified 145 local Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs marking 152 candidate Tbx5-dependent enhancers (empirical p<0.0001, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical significance and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Atrial open chromatin showed enrichment for motifs of TF families, such as MYC and E2F, that provide non-tissue-specific transcriptional functions.
source: Atrial open chromatin showed enrichment for motifs of TF families, such as MYC and E2F, that provide non-tissue-specific transcriptional functions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Tbx5-activated enhancers showed significant enrichment for the T-box motif itself (enrichment score = 6.7, p=0.03).
source: By contrast, Tbx5-activated enhancers showed significant enrichment for the T-box motif itself (enrichment score = 6.7, p=0.03, PWMEnrich [Frith et al., 2004]).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific statistical values.

claim: TBX5 occupancy by ChIP-seq in atrial HL-1 cells was highly enriched at open atrial locations that contained Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs (72 of the 152 locations, OR = 18, p<2e-16).
source: Furthermore, TBX5 occupancy by ChIP-seq in atrial HL-1 cells (He et al., 2011) was highly enriched at open atrial locations that contained Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs (72 of the 152 locations, OR = 18, p<2e-16; Fisher Exact Test, Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific statistical values and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: A candidate enhancer located at the Sln locus did not demonstrate TBX5 localization in ChIP-seq in HL-1 cells but did show Tbx5-dependent ncRNA transcription.
source: A candidate enhancer located at the Sln locus is one example: the region did not demonstrate TBX5 localization in ChIP-seq in HL-1 cells (He et al., 2011), but did show Tbx5-dependent ncRNA transcription.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an example of a false negative from ChIP-seq.

claim: The Sln locus region showed TBX5-occupancy by ChIP-qPCR (p=0.03 vs control Gapdh locus).
source: We interrogated this region by ChIP-qPCR and observed TBX5-occupancy (p=0.03 vs control Gapdh locus, two-tailed unequal variance t-test) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical values and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Sln element demonstrated robust TBX5-dependent activity in HL-1 cardiomyocytes in vitro (p = 2.3E-4 WT vs T-box Mutant).
source: The element demonstrated robust TBX5-dependent activity in HL-1 cardiomyocytes in vitro as determined by luciferase assay (p = 2.3E-4 WT vs T-box Mutant [two-tailed unequal variance t-test], Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical values and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 86% of downregulated (1577/1841; empirical p<0.001) Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were local to downregulated Tbx5-dependent coding-genes.
source: We observed that the direction of altered transcription of Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs and local polyA transcripts was most often coherent: 86% of downregulated (1577/1841; empirical p<0.001) and 66% of upregulated (1490/1769; empirical p=0.003) Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were local to downregulated and upregulated Tbx5-dependent coding-genes, respectively (Figure 1D,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific numbers and statistical values, shown in Figure 1D,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: 66% of upregulated (1490/1769; empirical p=0.003) Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were local to upregulated Tbx5-dependent coding-genes.
source: We observed that the direction of altered transcription of Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs and local polyA transcripts was most often coherent: 86% of downregulated (1577/1841; empirical p<0.001) and 66% of upregulated (1490/1769; empirical p=0.003) Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were local to downregulated and upregulated Tbx5-dependent coding-genes, respectively (Figure 1D,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific numbers and statistical values, shown in Figure 1D,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: 4C-Seq in the atrial HL-1 cardiomyocyte cell line demonstrated significant interactions between the enhancers defined by Tbx5-dependent transcription and local Tbx5-dependent genes located within topological associated domains at the genetic locations of Ryr2, Atp2a2, Ubc, and Wrn.
source: 4C-Seq in the atrial HL-1 cardiomyocyte cell line demonstrated significant interactions between the enhancers defined by Tbx5-dependent transcription and local Tbx5-dependent genes located within topological associated domains at the genetic locations of Ryr2, Atp2a2, Ubc, and Wrn (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 81 out of 93 enhancers with Tbx5-activated transcription showed quantitative directional coherence with the expression of the nearest Tbx5-dependent gene.
source: 81 out of 93 enhancers with Tbx5-activated transcription showed quantitative directional coherence with the expression of the nearest Tbx5-dependent gene (by Pi-score [Xiao et al., 2014]) (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A significant correlation was observed between the fold-changes of Tbx5-dependent enhancer transcription and that of adjacent Tbx5-dependent genes (coefficient = 0.58, p<2e-16 by Pearson Correlation test).
source: We analyzed the fold-changes of Tbx5-dependent enhancer transcription with that of adjacent Tbx5-dependent genes and observed a significant correlation between their direction and magnitude (coefficient = 0.58, p<2e-16 by Pearson Correlation test; Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific statistical values and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Gene Ontology enrichment analysis on the putative targets of enhancers that demonstrated Tbx5-activated transcription found enrichment for 'Calcium ion-related biological process' and 'Calcium ion transmembrane transport'.
source: We performed Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis (Wang et al., 2015) on the putative targets of enhancers that demonstrated Tbx5-activated transcription (Figure 4A). We found enrichment for two statistically significant terms, 'Calcium ion-related biological process' and 'Calcium ion transmembrane transport,' remarkably consistent with previous work demonstrating that Tbx5 controls atrial rhythm by driving calcium-handling physiology and gene expression (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The Ryr2 enhancer directed cardiac expression of an EGFP reporter in zebrafish lines with a stably integrated transgene.
source: Ryr2 directed cardiac expression of an EGFP reporter in zebrafish lines with a stably integrated transgene (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: Mutation of the seven canonical TBX5-binding sites within the Ryr2 enhancer diminished the frequency of cardiac expression in F0 zebrafish microinjected with the transgene construct (67/166 positive for wildtype vs 20/84 positive in the mutant and 5/95 for the Fos minimal promoter alone; p = 0.011, OR = 0.46 vs wildtype RACER).
source: To test whether expression activity was facilitated by T-box motifs, we mutated the seven canonical TBX5-binding sites located within the enhancer, which diminished the frequency of cardiac expression in F0 zebrafish microinjected with the transgene construct (67/166 positive for wildtype vs 20/84 positive in the mutant and 5/95 for the Fos minimal promoter alone; p = 0.011, OR = 0.46 vs wildtype RACER, Fisher's Exact Test) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific statistical values and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: The single candidate enhancer at Ryr2 marked by significant Tbx5-dependent ncRNA abundance showed strong cardiac activity as determined by luciferase assay (p = 0.05).
source: The single candidate enhancer marked by significant Tbx5-dependent ncRNA abundance showed strong cardiac activity as determined by luciferase assay (Figures 2C and 4D, p = 0.05, two-tailed unequal variance t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical values and shown in Figures 2C and 4D.

claim: The other candidate enhancers at Ryr2 showed weaker or no activity in HL-1 cardiomyocytes (p = 0.06, 0.39, 0.02 and 0.002 for Enhancers 1, 2, 3 and 5, respectively).
source: In contrast, the other candidates showed weaker or no activity in HL-1 cardiomyocytes (Figure 4C,D, p = 0.06, 0.39, 0.02 and 0.002 for Enhancers 1, 2, 3 and 5, respectively; two-tailed unequal variance t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical values and shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: RACER is located 25 kb upstream of the Ryr2 locus (mm9 chr13:12226210–12226916).
source: We refer to this lncRNA, located 25 kb upstream of the Ryr2 locus, as Ryr2 Associated Cis-Element RNA (mm9 chr13:12226210–12226916, RACER, Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific genomic coordinates and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Control knockdown of the Ryr2 mRNA caused a 50% reduction in Ryr2 mRNA abundance with no change in enhancer ncRNA expression.
source: Control knockdown of the Ryr2 mRNA caused a 50% reduction in Ryr2 mRNA abundance. Enhancer ncRNA expression was unchanged (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Knockdown of the Ryr2-enhancer-associated ncRNAs caused a 55% decrease in enhancer-associated ncRNA expression and a corresponding 50% decrease in Ryr2 mRNA abundance.
source: By contrast, knockdown of the Ryr2-enhancer-associated ncRNAs (chr13:12226210–12226916 mm9) caused a 55% decrease in enhancer-associated ncRNA expression and, importantly, a corresponding 50% decrease in Ryr2 mRNA abundance (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: In untransfected HL-1 cells, β-adrenergic stimulus (1 nM isoproterenol, ISO) caused a dramatic increase in the increase rate of cytosolic calcium transients (rate change from 33.3 ± 7.4 to 84.8 ± 9.9, p<0.05).
source: In untransfected HL-1 cells, β-adrenergic stimulus (1 nM isoproterenol, ISO) caused a dramatic increase in the increase rate of cytosolic calcium transients (rate change from 33.3 ± 7.4 to 84.8 ± 9.9, p<0.05, two-tailed unequal variance t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific values and statistical significance.

claim: Control Ryr2-mRNA-knockdown blunted the effect of β-adrenergic stimulus (increase rate change from 34.8 ± 5.9 to 33.3 ± 7.4 p = NS).
source: Control Ryr2-mRNA-knockdown blunted the effect of β-adrenergic stimulus (increase rate change from 34. 8 ± 5.9 to 33.3 ± 7.4 p = NS, Fisher's Exact Test) (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific values and shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: Knockdown of RACER blocked the effect of ISO (increase rate change 49.3 ± 11.3 to 41.0 ± 6.1; p = NS).
source: Knockdown of RACER blocked the effect of ISO, mimicking the effect of direct Ryr2 knockdown. (increase rate change 49.3 ± 11.3 to 41.0 ± 6.1; p = NS, Fisher's Exact Test) (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific values and shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: Six Tbx5-dependent enhancer lncRNAs, including RACER, were all significantly enriched in the chromatin versus the soluble nuclear fraction (qPCR p<6e-3, n = 3).
source: We found that the Tbx5-dependent lncRNAs were all significantly enriched in the chromatin versus the soluble nuclear fraction (qPCR p<6e-3, n = 3 two-tailed unequal variance t-test) (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical values and shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Control RNA from the Gapdh-coding region showed no chromatin enrichment.
source: By contrast, control RNA from the Gapdh-coding region showed no chromatin enrichment.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a negative control.

claim: Xist demonstrated a degree of chromatin enrichment similar to that of the examined Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs.
source: Xist, a canonical chromatin-binding ncRNA, served as a positive control and demonstrated a degree of chromatin enrichment similar to that of the examined Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Knockdown of RACER caused a quantitatively significant fall in Pol2 occupancy at the Ryr2 promoter (Pol2 ChIP enriched vs ctrl locus 8.7 ± 0.79 fold vs 1.6 ± 0.20 fold in knockdown, p = 0.02).
source: Knockdown of RACER caused a quantitatively significant fall in Pol2 occupancy at the Ryr2 promoter, suggesting that this enhancer-bourne lncRNA is necessary for recruiting or stabilizing Pol2 at the target gene (Pol2 ChIP enriched vs ctrl locus 8.7 ± 0.79 fold vs 1.6 ± 0.20 fold in knockdown, p = 0.02, two-tailed unequal variance t-test, Figure 4J).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific values and shown in Figure 4J.

claim: There was no change in Pol2 occupancy at the housekeeping gene Btf3 after RACER knockdown (21.3 ± 5.99 fold vs 14.3 ± 4.85 fold, p = 0.46).
source: There was no change in Pol2 occupancy at the housekeeping gene Btf3 after RACER knockdown (21.3 ± 5.99 fold vs 14.3 ± 4.85 fold, p = 0.46, two-tailed unequal variance t-test, Figure 4J).
evidence: This is stated in the results with specific values and shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Enhancer-bourne ncRNAs mark active cis-regulatory elements.
source: Taken in context, this work contributes to the concepts that enhancer-bourne ncRNAs (1) mark active cis-regulatory elements and (2) are essential for cis-regulatory element function (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the work.

claim: Enhancer-bourne ncRNAs are essential for cis-regulatory element function.
source: Taken in context, this work contributes to the concepts that enhancer-bourne ncRNAs (1) mark active cis-regulatory elements and (2) are essential for cis-regulatory element function (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the work.

claim: The differential ncRNA approach provides non-redundant data when compared with other current state-of-the-art methods that attempt to define enhancers by proxy, using genomic accessibility or histone status.
source: The differential ncRNA approach appears to provide non-redundant data when compared with other current state-of-the-art methods that attempt to define enhancers by proxy, using genomic accessibility (e.g. DNAse-seq or ATAC-seq) or histone status (e.g. H3K27ac).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Differential TF-dependent ncRNA-seq may provide a direct readout of differential enhancer function.
source: The quantitative correlation between the RNA abundance of the enhancer and that of the target promoter that we observed (Figure 3C) suggests that differential TF-dependent ncRNA-seq may provide a direct readout of differential enhancer function (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: All validated Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were also cheRNAs.
source: We observed that all validated Tbx5-dependent ncRNAs were also cheRNAs (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 4I.

claim: CheRNAs have been shown to act locally to promote proximal gene transcription in a tissue-specific fashion.
source: CheRNAs have been shown to act locally to promote proximal gene transcription in a tissue-specific fashion (Werner and Ruthenburg, 2015; Werner et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation support.

claim: The dependence of target gene transcription on enhancer transcription may be a fundamental aspect of TF-driven cis-regulatory networks.
source: The dependence of target gene transcription on enhancer transcription may be a fundamental aspect of TF-driven cis-regulatory networks (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation based on the findings.

claim: Enhancer-associated RNAs are canonically under poly-adenylated.
source: To identify TBX5-dependent noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs), we sequenced non-polyadenylated RNA from the atrium of control (R26CreERt2; n = 3) and Tbx5 mutant (Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERt2; n = 4) adult mice, as enhancer-associated RNAs are canonically under poly-adenylated (Kim et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation support.

claim: ncRNAs are highly tissue-specific.
source: This observation is consistent with the observation that ncRNAs are highly tissue-specific and that global ncRNA discovery has not been previously reported in the atrium of the heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Quinn and Chang, 2016).

claim: Open chromatin is a global feature of enhancers.
